from_notes: It ruled that right to privacy is protected as an intrinsic part of right to life and personal liberty under Article 21
x: In K.S. Puttaswamy v Union of India (2017) the Supreme Court held privacy protected as an intrinsic part of life and personal liberty under Article 21 and as part of the freedoms of Part III. Articles 20, 22 and 23 deal with conviction, detention and forced labour.
source: Laxmikanth 8th ed. Vol. 3 (src/polity/laxmikanth-indian-polity-03.txt) p.42: 'protected as an intrinsic part of right to life and personal liberty under Article 21 and as a part of the freedoms guaranteed by Part III'

from_notes: Name of the Case: K.S. Puttaswamy vs. Union of India; Popular Name: Right to privacy case
x: The 2017 privacy case was filed by Justice K.S. Puttaswamy (Retd); it overruled M.P. Sharma (1954) and Kharak Singh (1962) insofar as they denied privacy. PUCL (1997) dealt with telephone interception.
source: Laxmikanth 8th ed. Vol. 3 (src/polity/laxmikanth-indian-polity-03.txt) p.42 (Name of the Case: K.S. Puttaswamy vs. Union of India, Right to privacy case)
